title: LastTake
tagline: Durable Strands interrupts preserve a scene's evidence until the right human can resume the wrap decision.
inspiration: Durable Strands interrupts preserve a scene's evidence until the right human can resume the wrap decision. At the end of a shoot day, the evidence needed to judge whether a scene is ready to wrap is scattered across the current script, shot list, captured takes, script supervisor's notes, camera and sound reports, continuity references and release ledger. Nobody holds all of it at once. LastTake makes missing or conflicting records visible while the script supervisor can still review them. The project uses a synthetic scene and has no observed crew trial, time saving, avoided pickup or cost result.
what_it_does: LastTake is a second set of eyes for the script supervisor and a safe decision packet for the 1st AD. When a user or API client requests a wrap checkpoint, that request records scene.wrap-checkpoint.requested on EventBridge and then starts the Strands orchestrator directly; no EventBridge rule or subscriber triggers the workflow today. Four bounded checks reconcile the supplied records: coverage (required beats against captured takes), continuity (preferred takes that would constrain the edit), metadata (slate, media, sound and lens reconciliation) and rights (every person and visible asset traced to a release or licence). A deterministic gate with no model in it combines the findings and either refuses or emits an eligibility result. Two material transitions, the pickup and the wrap, suspend the run with a real Strands interrupt and wait for a named human role; a later request can resume the run in a different process from the session stored on S3. An approved action publishes one EventBridge event under an idempotency key. The system records bus acceptance, not downstream delivery. A sealed, versioned turnover is saved and exposed in Handoff for download, with every accepted exception still on it. Absent evidence is a finding, never a pass. The product may not judge creative quality, may not declare anything legally cleared, and may not approve a wrap. Those stay with people, and the interface says so.
how_we_built_it: Strands Agents SDK on AWS Lambda (arm64) behind an API Gateway HTTP API; Aurora DSQL for run state, sealed findings, decisions and handled events; S3 for content-addressed supplied artifacts, suspended Strands sessions and turnover manifests; EventBridge for approved actions; and a React workspace served as static files from S3 through CloudFront. The deterministic gate verifies each finding's seal and cited source digests before using it. Decisions, audit entries and handled events are not sealed records. The hosted browser uses a scripted planner and offline lexical interpreter. A separate owner-dispatched backend deployment check invokes Amazon Bedrock through the same interpreter port; Bedrock is not active in the hosted browser path. The current public frontend release came from GitHub Actions. After 26 desktop and mobile browser journeys succeed against the live URL, that workflow publishes an acceptance receipt naming the observed frontend and backend commits; a failed run does not overwrite the prior receipt.
challenges: Strands replays a tool body from its first line on resume, so any external effect placed before the interrupt fires twice; every approved action now sits after the interrupt behind an idempotency key, proven in a browser by approving, counting pickup.requested, resending the identical approval and counting again. Writing the ablation exposed fail-open paths: an unknown continuity result blocked nothing, and the rollup credited a viable take despite the coverage check. Both are fixed and pinned. The current rerunnable ablation takes coverage from 31 of 34 to 0 of 34 when the interpreter is unreachable (PYTHONPATH=src python tools/ablation.py). Human decisions are bound to the digest of the finding they were taken about, so an approval expires when the evidence moves and the page says which one and why. Screens that described intent rather than deployed behaviour were found by reading the deployed page and removed; the uptime check now greps the served bundle for those sentences.
accomplishments: Of 34 required beats in the fictional scene, the checkpoint reports 31 covered with evidence, 2 raising exceptions with named sources, and 1 with no release record routed to production (python -m pytest tests/test_corpus_counts.py). A recorded backend deployment test exercised pause and resume across different Lambda containers (GitHub Actions run 32606395610); source CI independently exercises two operating-system processes. A frontend release does not repeat the Lambda proof. A person can supply a take or a release record from the browser, see the findings change, and see a prior approval withdrawn when the evidence it was about moves. Handoff exposes a sealed manifest and portable receipt that carry their own run, policy version and open items.
what_we_learned: Several defects were found only by reading deployed output: a browser test on the live URL, a curl of the API, or a grep of the served bundle. Absent evidence has to be a finding at every layer, including the interface, or a reassuring screen becomes the failure.
what_is_next: Bedrock on the public path once its semantic value over the lexical reader is measured against the frozen cases already prepared (docs/model-evidence-protocol.json); one real production input format with a safe preview; a bounded offline experience for a set with no signal; and the walkthrough by a practising script supervisor that no automated journey replaces.
limits_stated_plainly: The corpus is synthetic: THE LAST FERRY is a fictional production and the packet says so on its face.
No footage or audio is analysed. Sound checks reconcile supplied metadata only.
Nothing is legally cleared by this system; a verified rights row means the expected record was found and its fields matched policy.
No practising script supervisor has run it. Automated journeys are not user validation.
Human active time, interruptions and corrections are unmeasured; timing a model and calling it human time saved would be a fabricated benchmark.
aws_services: Amazon Bedrock (supported through the interpreter port; not active on the public deployment)

All AWS adapters, Strands agent definitions, the gate, the checks, the corpus and the interface are new. Details in README, Pre-existing components.
